question.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2\}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:      

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+x{y}^{2}]}_{-1}^{1}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[(\frac{1}{3}+{y}^{2})-(-\frac{1}{3}-{y}^{2})]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{2}{3}+2{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{2}{3}+2{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y & ={[\frac{2y}{3}+\frac{2{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(2+{2}^{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{20}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
